_readme: SHARED GOLDEN FIXTURE — spec §12. Byte-identical duplicate in BOTH prep/tests/fixtures/ and template/tests/fixtures/. Locks prep's Python port `narrow_obligations_pure` (generate_template_config.py) against §9a's TypeScript original `narrowObligationsPure` (tools/narrowObligations.ts). A silent divergence here would be WORSE than the bug it replaces: prep would certify a demo trigger the shipped guardrail then declines to narrow, and the demo would fail exactly where the spec claims it cannot. Asserted by test_generate_template_config.py::test_narrowing_golden_parity and narrowObligations.test.ts::test_narrowing_golden_parity. firmProfile keys are camelCase (`impactedFunctions`) per FirmProfileSchema; clearedSet records are snake_case ClearedRecords per §5. urgencyWeight is relative to SNAPSHOT_DATE 2026-07-11 (never Date.now()): <= 180 days -> 2 (boundary 2027-01-07), else 1; null -> 0. EDIT BOTH COPIES OR NEITHER.

cases.name: jurisdiction_required_no_match_excludes_everything
cases.note: A firm outside a record's jurisdiction is categorically irrelevant — no exceptions, however strong the topical overlap. These records have PERFECT industry AND function overlap and are still excluded.

cases.name: supranational_scope_alone_never_matches
cases.note: §9a's fix: `scope === 'supranational'` alone was admitting obligations with no real connection to the firm. The BLOC IDENTITIES must actually agree. Here the record's bloc is EU and the firm's bloc is null.

cases.name: bloc_match_when_country_differs
cases.note: Second branch of jurisdictionMatches: bloc identities agree.

cases.name: topical_required_jurisdiction_only_match_is_excluded
cases.note: Required-AND semantics. Jurisdiction matches perfectly; neither industry nor function overlaps. Excluded.

cases.name: function_overlap_alone_is_sufficient
cases.note: Topical relevance can come from EITHER dimension — a record can be functionally relevant without a literal industry-tag match.

cases.name: overlap_is_case_insensitive
cases.note: Tag capitalization is not guaranteed consistent across the corpus.

cases.name: ranking_by_overlap_count
cases.note: rankOf = industry overlap + function overlap + urgencyWeight. All compliance_dates null (urgencyWeight 0) so overlap alone orders these.

cases.name: urgency_weight_boundary_at_exactly_180_days
cases.note: THE boundary. SNAPSHOT_DATE=2026-07-11. 2027-01-07 is exactly 180 days out -> weight 2. 2027-01-08 is 181 -> weight 1. A `< 180` implementation, or one using Date.now(), fails this case.

cases.name: tie_break_sooner_deadline_first
cases.note: Equal rankOf (both weight 2, same overlaps) -> sooner date first.

cases.name: tie_break_final_by_id_ascending
cases.note: Same rankOf, same compliance_date -> id ascending. The final deterministic tie-break; without it the order is sort-stability luck.

cases.name: more_than_five_matches_truncates_to_top_five
cases.note: Ranking, not just the gate, is exercised: seven relevant records, the five with the nearest compliance dates survive, in date order.

cases.name: irrelevant_record_never_crowds_out_a_relevant_one
cases.note: §9a's central fix. Six jurisdiction-mismatched records cannot occupy a slot however high their other signals; the one relevant record wins.

cases.name: empty_cleared_set
cases.note: Zero candidates -> the processor returns the draft unchanged (§9a).
